newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Oct 1.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Oct 1.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

Coles Myer early on Tuesday posted a net profit of A$280.4 million for the 52 weeks to July 28, 1996, down 33.8 percent on the previous year. It said it does not expect any short term improvement in the difficult retail environment across Australia. It said also that after a strategic review of its World 4 Kids toy chain, it had decided to keep some stand alone World 4 Kids stores.

Fox Kids Worldwide Inc, part of News Corp, said overnight in the United States it filed for an initial public offering of common stock. Fox Kids, which produces the "Mighty Morphin Power Rangers", did not release terms of the planned offering, but said all shares are being sold by the company.

Labor talks at Kennecott Copper in Utah were continuing as the midnight local time expiry of the existing three-year deal neared. Kennecott, a subsidiary of RTZ-CRA, has been negotiating with seven international unions and 17 local unions. Some 1,800 Kennecott workers are represented by unions at the 310,000 short tons-a-year copper refinery.

Also overnight in the United States Lenfest Communications Inc said it and News Corp had settled lawsuits against each other over an alleged oral agreement related to the recapitalisation of pay tv operator Australis Media Ltd . The lawsuits were settled by agreeing to dismiss all claims without payment of any damages, Lenfest said.

Australian National Industries Ltd (ANI) said late on Monday it had revoked the power of a board committee which was inquiring into ANI's purchase of the Holter environmental group in Germany and had appointed lawyer Robert Ellicott to handle the inquiries. ANI managing director Peter Stancliffe later told Reuters he planned to issue a statement this week about the boardroom dispute.

U.K. life assurance to investment company Guinness Peat Group said on Monday it was in acquisition talks with Gowrings, the UK motor dealerships to fast food outlets company in which it has a 14 percent stake. Guinness Peat said it hoped to extend weekend talks with a view to secure a recommendation from Gowrings at a price of not less than 90 pence per share cash with a loan note alternative.

Auspine Ltd said on Monday that director Rodney Hartley had resigned from the board, citing a breakdown in its operations. "Mr Hartley's reason for his resignation, given to the board this afternoon, is that an irretrievable breakdown in the operations of the board had occurred," Auspine said in a statement to the Australian Stock Exchange.

G.U.D. Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday it had bought automotive filter manufacturers Wesfil Australia Pty Ltd and Wesfil Filters Pty Ltd for an undisclosed price. The two firms have combined annual revenues of A$8 million.
